subject: Game-time decision
title: What does game-time decision mean? Sports injury term, explained
answer: A game-time decision means a team will not decide whether an injured player will play until shortly before the game starts. In the NFL, that usually means a player listed as "questionable" whose status is settled at the inactive list deadline, 90 minutes before kickoff.
in_the_news: Every weekend, coaches call a key player a game-time decision, and fantasy football managers have to guess whether to start him.
body:
Coaches use the phrase when a player is hurt but might be able to go. The final call usually comes after a pregame workout, when trainers check whether the player can run, cut and take contact without pain. Some teams also use the label to keep the opponent guessing.

In the NFL, teams file an official injury report during the week. A player listed as "questionable" is uncertain to play; "doubtful" means unlikely; "out" means he will not play. The game-time decision is settled when teams turn in their list of inactive players, which is due 90 minutes before kickoff. For a 1 p.m. Eastern game, that is 11:30 a.m. Eastern.

For fantasy football, that timing matters most for late games: if a player in a late kickoff is a game-time decision, managers often start a backup from a later game, or a player whose status is already certain. In the NBA, the similar step is the official status update teams send before tipoff.

faq.q: What does game day decision mean
faq.a: The same as a game-time decision: the team will decide on the day of the game, shortly before it starts, whether the player is healthy enough to play.
Teams must submit their inactive lists 90 minutes before kickoff.

faq.q: Should I start a game-time decision in fantasy football
faq.a: It depends on the kickoff time. Check the inactive list 90 minutes before the game; if the player's game is late, consider a reliable backup.
